cf.title: EXPLAIN ANALYZE overcounts MERGE inserts suppressed by triggers

input.subject: EXPLAIN ANALYZE overcounts MERGE inserts suppressed by triggers

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. Message #1 states the bug, gives a reproducer and explains why the caller cannot count correctly. The fix moves an existing counter and adds no user surface. Confidence is low because only one message is visible and the code was not read.

brief.title: Fix EXPLAIN ANALYZE MERGE insert count when a trigger skips the row
brief.problem: When a BEFORE INSERT trigger returns NULL for a MERGE insert, EXPLAIN ANALYZE still reports `Tuples Inserted: 1` and `Tuples Skipped: 0`, though the target table stays empty. Users who read MERGE statistics in EXPLAIN ANALYZE get wrong counts.
brief.proposed_design: The patch moves the mt_merge_inserted increment from ExecMergeNotMatched() into ExecInsert(), after the row is inserted or queued for FDW batch insertion. The caller cannot tell from the returned NULL slot whether the insert happened. ExecInsert() checks the current MERGE action so the insert half of a cross-partition UPDATE counts only as an UPDATE.
user_visible_surface: EXPLAIN ANALYZE output for MERGE: `Tuples Inserted` and `Tuples Skipped` change when a BEFORE INSERT trigger suppresses the row.
author_claims: ExecInsert() returns NULL both for a trigger-suppressed insert and for a successful insert without RETURNING, so the caller cannot count correctly.
ExecInsert() control flow already separates skipped rows from inserted or FDW-batched rows.
Cross-partition UPDATE inside MERGE is still counted only as an UPDATE.
The extended merge.sql trigger test checks the inserted and skipped counts.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. Nobody has replied yet.
unclear: The material does not say which branches have the bug or whether the fix is meant for back-patching.
The author does not say whether ON CONFLICT or INSERT ... SELECT paths through ExecInsert() are affected by the moved increment.
The thread does not say whether an FDW batch row that the remote side later rejects or skips is still counted as inserted.
The author does not say whether MATCHED UPDATE and DELETE actions have the same problem with BEFORE triggers.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry is tagged Bugfix, and a back-patch would change EXPLAIN ANALYZE counts for MERGE in released branches.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: ExecInsert(), shared by all insert paths, gains a check of the current MERGE action.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a check in ExecInsert(), which every inserted row passes through.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which branches have the wrong count, and do you propose to back-patch the fix?
How does ExecInsert() tell a MERGE insert action from a plain INSERT, INSERT ... SELECT or ON CONFLICT call, so that those paths leave mt_merge_inserted unchanged?
Is a row queued for FDW batch insertion counted as inserted if the remote side later rejects or skips it?
Do MATCHED UPDATE and DELETE actions report wrong counts when a BEFORE trigger returns NULL?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the MERGE executor code in nodeModifyTable.c, including the cross-partition UPDATE and FDW batch insert paths, would have to own it. Nobody has replied yet.
committability.liability: The owner signs for correct MERGE counts across all ExecInsert() callers, and for any change in EXPLAIN ANALYZE output on back branches if the fix is back-patched.
committability.author_follow_up: No sign either way; the thread has one message.

priority.reason: The bug affects users who read EXPLAIN ANALYZE counts for MERGE on tables with a BEFORE INSERT trigger that returns NULL. The patch is 4.3 KB, touches one executor file plus the merge regression test, and adds no user surface.

provisional_note: Without the code, three points are unchecked: the ON CONFLICT and plain INSERT paths through ExecInsert(), the count for FDW batch rows the remote side rejects, and the cross-partition UPDATE check.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW
precedents_retrieved.summary: Allow EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE on REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, showing the plan of the view's defining SELECT (plain EXPLAIN without refreshing, EXPLAIN ANALYZE performing the refresh), analogous to existing EXPLAIN support for CREATE TABLE AS / CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW. A companion patch refactored ExecRefreshMatView into smaller functions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that supporting EXPLAIN would bind REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW to having an explainable SQL plan, constraining future implementations such as incremental view maintenance, while offering little beyond explaining the view's query directly; the author agreed to withdraw the feature. The leftover refactoring patch was also not taken, because John Naylor judged it would conflict with the refactoring in the pending incremental view maintenance patch without helping it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The problem with it is that it
binds us to the assumption that REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW has an
explainable plan.

precedents_retrieved.title: Sampling-based timing for EXPLAIN ANALYZE
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a TIMING SAMPLING mode to EXPLAIN ANALYZE that records a timestamp from a recurring timer (up to 1000 Hz) instead of reading the clock in InstrStartNode/InstrStopNode. Each node's sampled time is scaled to total wall clock time to keep overhead close to TIMING OFF.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread went stale after January and the patch stopped building on the CFBot, so Daniel Gustafsson returned it with feedback. Earlier review asked whether sampling still pays off once the RDTSC patch lands. It also noted that fast nodes get zero sampled time, and suggested hybrid designs that time early or rarely called nodes exactly; the author did not post a new version.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This thread has been stale since January with no movement at all during the
March CF, and according to the CFBot it stopped building at all ~ 14 weeks ago.

precedents_retrieved.title: Summary Sort workers Stats in EXPLAIN ANALYZE
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes EXPLAIN ANALYZE so that Sort node statistics from parallel workers are summarized (average and peak sort space used, sort method, number of workers) instead of being printed per worker. This follows the approach already used by show_incremental_sort_group_info() and is meant to reduce output size when many workers are used.
precedents_retrieved.objection: After a review pointing out issues (summary only in non-VERBOSE mode, reporting workers planned rather than launched, unclear text format), the author posted a revised patch, but the patch later failed regression tests on all platforms. A reviewer asked for an updated patch, none was posted, and the entry was marked Returned with Feedback for lack of an update.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This has been marked as RwF based on the lack of an update.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reduce timing overhead of EXPLAIN ANALYZE using rdtsc
precedents_retrieved.authors: Andres Freund (andresfreund), Lukas Fittl (lfittl), David Geier (geidav)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make instr_time count CPU reference cycles read with rdtsc, which does not wait for prior instructions, and convert cycles to time only on output, to cut the timing overhead of EXPLAIN ANALYZE. The patch uses rdtsc only on Linux/x86 when the kernel clocksource is tsc, takes the TSC frequency from CPUID, and falls back to clock_gettime() otherwise.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread stopped after the v8 patch of February 2023, and nobody continued the work for about a year. vignesh C closed the entry as Returned with feedback because neither the author nor anyone else took it forward. Earlier, Andres Freund doubted the patch was ready on reliability and code complexity, citing the Linux-only restriction, but the entry closed from inactivity.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since the author or no one else showed interest in taking it forward
and the patch had no activity for more than 1 year, I have changed the
status to RWF.

precedents_retrieved.title: MERGE SQL command
precedents_retrieved.authors: Álvaro Herrera (alvherre), Simon Riggs (simon), Pavan Deolasee (pavan)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Alvaro Herrera rebased Simon Riggs and Pavan Deolasee's patch implementing the SQL MERGE command, which applies conditional INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE actions to a target table based on a join with a source. The patch adds parser, planner, executor (ExecMerge in nodeModifyTable.c) and documentation support, with foreign tables not supported and rewrite rules ignored.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch received review comments (documentation clarity, executor structure, silent ignoring of rewrite rules, an uninitialized variable in ExecDelete) but no updated version followed for the next commitfests. When the patch no longer applied in the 2021-09 commitfest, the author said no new version would be coming and asked to close the entry, planning to open a new one later.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
No, sorry, there won't.  I think it's better to close it as RfW at this
point, I'll create a new one when I have it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Restrict EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) for RLS and security_barrier views
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch forbids EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) for statements that use row-level security or security_barrier views, so ordinary users cannot see how many rows the policy or view condition filtered out. Only members of a predefined role, proposed as pg_read_all_stats, could still run it in those cases.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Dean Rasheed noted that the issue is not a security bug and that row counts can also be seen through pg_stat_get_tuples_returned(), pg_class.reltuples and plain EXPLAIN estimates, so EXPLAIN should stay as it is. After a discussion on pgsql-security, the author marked the patch rejected. The reason was that a determined attacker who can run arbitrary SQL can subvert row-level security anyway, so the restriction makes performance analysis harder without a real security gain.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Therefore, restricting EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) will do more harm than good, since it will make analyzing query performance harder without a real security gain.

precedents_retrieved.title: intXshr, intXshl: return error on shift count out of range
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the integer shift functions (int4shl, int4shr and their siblings) raise a "shift count out of range" error when the shift count is at least the bit width of the type. The author argued that such shifts are undefined behaviour in C and give different results on x86, ARM and RISC-V, and claimed RISC-V crashes.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane held that these functions exist to give access to the C bitwise operators with whatever behaviour the platform has, and that restricting them would break code that works today. Tests on RISC-V hardware by Tom Lane and Alexander Lakhin showed no crash, and the author withdrew that claim. David Rowley agreed, noted that masking the count would still leave signed overflow platform-dependent, and wrote a documentation patch instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There is no contract to restrict
them to some guaranteed-portable functionality subset, and I think
trying to do that would accomplish little except to break code that
had been working fine in the context it's used in.

precedents_retrieved.title: Enhance file_fdw to report processed and skipped tuples in COPY progress
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes file_fdw report tuples_processed and tuples_skipped (rows skipped with on_error = 'ignore') in pg_stat_progress_copy. file_fdw already reports some columns there, such as relid and bytes_processed.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Masahiko Sawada noted that file_fdw's use of COPY progress does not work well, because one query can run several file_fdw scans at once and each backend has only one progress slot. The author first argued this was a separate, existing problem, then withdrew the patch: wider COPY progress support in file_fdw would make wrong progress reports more common.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don’t think the fact that the issue
already exists is a good reason to introduce more, and likely more common,
scenarios where it could occur.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the retrieved list has no earlier attempt at this fix or a close relative, and message #1 points to no earlier discussion. From the prior-attempts angle there is no rejection reason to carry over.

From the standards and compatibility angle, the only user-visible change is that EXPLAIN ANALYZE for MERGE reports `Tuples Inserted` and `Tuples Skipped` correctly when a BEFORE INSERT trigger suppresses a row. The patch adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object or psql change, and nothing in pg_dump is affected. A committer may still ask whether to back-patch, since tools or tests that saved the old counts would see them change.

The patch changes only an in-memory executor counter that EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows. It does not touch on-disk format, WAL, replication, catalogs, the wire protocol or extension structs. A field mt_merge_inserted that already exists is updated in a different function, so nothing persists or crosses a process boundary.

The patch only changes the MERGE insert and skip counters that EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows to the user who ran the statement. It adds no privilege, role, setting or new exposure, so there is no security angle to object on.

From the maintenance and fit angle, this is a narrow executor bugfix with no hot-path cost, catalog, GUC, API or external dependency. Moving the counter into ExecInsert() adds MERGE awareness to a shared function, but it fixes a wrong count without a new mechanism. Three points cannot be checked without the code: the ON CONFLICT paths, rows the remote side rejects after FDW batching, and back-patch scope.

This is a bug fix to EXPLAIN ANALYZE counters for MERGE. No existing feature, extension or setting corrects the wrong count. The patch changes the existing mt_merge_inserted counter and does not add a second mechanism, so the already-exists angle has nothing to raise.

This is a bug fix: EXPLAIN ANALYZE reports a wrong MERGE insert count, and message #1 gives a reproducer. The demand test does not apply to correcting existing output, and the fix adds no user surface for anyone else to pay for.
